title: Nested contents and offline chapter search

fields.outcome: A reader of a long HTML manual can see chapters nested by heading depth and can search headings, prose, captions, and alt text from the page itself, then open the matching chapter.
fields.scope: Render the HTML contents list from headingLevel, nesting a section under the nearest earlier section with a smaller level. Add a search box whose index is embedded in the file and covers headings, text, captions, and alt text. Group results under the top-level section, show a highlighted snippet and the heading path, and move through results with the keyboard to the section anchor. Exclude topics, cross-references, breadcrumbs, previous and next links, collapsible chapters, branding, language switching, and PDF bookmarks.
fields.acceptance: A level 2 chapter is listed inside the preceding level 1 part. Search for words that appear only in a caption shows that chapter, grouped under its part, with the match highlighted, and does not request another file. Arrow keys and Enter open the section. A heading containing markup stays text.
fields.decisions: Use the existing headingLevel for parts instead of a new part field. One result per matching section. Keep the search script and index inline so a single HTML file can search with no network request. English search label matches the current HTML language.
fields.verification: Run the documentation generator tests and a browser check that nests the contents list, searches a caption, and opens the result from the keyboard.
fields.dependencies: Uses the existing HTML generator and section headingLevel.
fields.risks: A viewer that blocks inline scripts still shows the contents links, but the search box does not run. Search does not group by topic.

criteria.expectation: The HTML contents list nests each section under the nearest earlier section with a smaller headingLevel.
Search matches headings, prose, captions, and alt text from an index in the file and does not request another file.
A result shows the heading path, a highlighted snippet, and the top-level section, and links to the section anchor.
Arrow keys move through the results and Enter opens the selected section.
A heading that contains markup is escaped in the contents list and cannot break out of the search index.
